newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may bankrupt Nizhnevartovsk - agencies.
newsitem.headline: Russia may bankrupt Nizhnevartovsk - agencies.

text.p: The Russian government will not allow oil company AOOT Nizhnevartovskneftegaz to restructure its tax debts and has decided to initiate bankruptcy proceedings against it, a spokesman for Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.
Chubais announced the decision at a meeting of the government's commission on current issues, which was discussing the fate of major corporate tax debtors, Andrei Trapeznikov said.

As of May 1, Nizhnevartovskneftegaz owed 1.17 trillion roubles ($203.1 million) in taxes, State Tax Service figures show. Nizhnevartovskneftegaz is the main production unit of Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (TNK) (Tyumen Oil). Earlier on Tuesday the government announced an investment tender for 40 percent of TNK next month.

The cash-strapped government is forcing major corporate tax debtors to restructure their tax, by issuing either shares or asset-backed bonds to the government which can be sold if companies default on a schedule of tax payments.

The commission, chaired by Chubais in his role as First Deputy Prime Minister in charge of economic policy, approved restructuring plans for carmaker AvtoVAZ and oil companies Yuganskneftegaz and Samaraneftegaz, and Norilsk Nickel's flagship plant Norilsky Gorno-Metallurgichesky Kombinat (NGMK), Russian news agencies said.
At 1200 GMT Nizhnevartovskneftegaz was $8.30 on the Russian Trading System, down from $10.00 at Monday's close.
